seo.description: Walk the Skala de la Ville in Essaouira: historic cannons, Atlantic panoramas and the classic postcard viewpoint above the medina walls.
seo.keywords: Skala de la Ville, Essaouira cannons, ramparts viewpoint, Mogador Skala, Atlantic walls

name: Skala de la Ville
hero_subtitle: The cannon platform above the Atlantic — Essaouira’s most iconic rampart walk.

overview.title: Cannons facing the swell
overview.p1: The Skala de la Ville is the raised artillery platform on Essaouira’s seaward walls. Old bronze cannons point at the Atlantic; below, waves hit the rocks and gulls ride the wind.
overview.p2: It is short, dramatic and almost always windy. Steady shoes help on uneven stone. Sunset draws a crowd — come a little earlier for space.
overview.p3: Pair it with the medina lanes and, if energy remains, the Skala du Port for a full rampart circuit.

food.title: Food near the Skala
food.p1: Drop back into the medina for cafés after the ramparts, or continue to the port for grilled fish.
food.li1: Medina cafés a few minutes inland from the Skala.
food.li2: Port fish stalls for a casual lunch.
food.li3: Quiet square restaurants off the main lane.
food.li4: Carry water — the cannon platform is fully exposed.
food.p2: Evenings cool quickly when the wind rises.

tips.title: Practical tips for Skala de la Ville

1.title: Access
1.desc: Reach it through the medina; follow signs or the sound of the sea.

2.title: Wind & sun
2.desc: Very exposed to wind and sun — jacket and high SPF.

3.title: Safety
3.desc: Mind the drop toward the rocks; keep children close.

faq.title: FAQ about Skala de la Ville

q1.question: Is entry free?
q1.answer: Yes. The platform is a public rampart walk.

q2.question: How long?
q2.answer: 45 to 90 minutes including photos and pauses.

q3.question: Best light?
q3.answer: Late afternoon and sunset for colour; morning for fewer people.

q4.question: Very windy?
q4.answer: Almost always — that is part of the experience.

q5.question: Combine with the port Skala?
q5.answer: Yes. Many visitors do both the same day.
